subject: Media Literacy
title: Encryption and Government Access
description: A quick, practical guide to Encryption and Government Access.

hook.text: The FBI asked Apple to unlock a terrorist's iPhone. Apple refused, arguing it would compromise everyone's security.

buildup.text: Encryption scrambles data so only intended recipients can read it. Governments want backdoor access for investigations.

discovery.text: Strong encryption protects journalists, activists, and dissidents. It also protects criminals. The same technology serves both.

twist.text: Security experts agree: a backdoor for governments is a backdoor for hackers. You can't make a lock only good people can pick.

climax.text: The encryption debate pits security against security — national security versus personal cybersecurity.

punchline.text: A door only the government can open is a door anyone will eventually open.

quiz.question: Why do security experts oppose encryption backdoors?
options: A backdoor for governments is also a vulnerability that hackers can exploit
